items.title: Gerald Wiggins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 2, 1995
items.q: I gave him my notice right then and there. And he said, “Okay.” And that was the end of it. And J.J. Johnson and Max Roach they say, “Oh Wig, come on” you know. So a couple of days later I went to Benny and I said, “About that notice I gave you I’d like to take it back.

ctx.x: How about the best road experience you had, either with Les Hite or anybody from—

Well I had fun with all the gigs I had, with the singers and the bands, you know. There were good times and bad times. I think the worst time I had was when I joined Louis Armstrong. I joined Louis out here, and we made 50 one nighters, all through the south. And at that time the south was pretty bad. So two weeks before we got to New York, I put in my notice. I loved the band and everything but I just couldn’t stand what we were going through. It wasn’t very nice. Anyhow we got to New York and I was home about…
Was there a difference in that tour than with Louis?
